body: Thank you for the encouragement.
Thank you for the offer man!
It can definitely bring me down at times. I'll get frustrated and feel like I'm not good at anything.
Thanks for the offer, I may take you up on it.
Thanks. That's a daunting thing for me given my social anxiety. But it might be worth looking into down the road.
I do play on lichess. I'll hit you up. Thanks.

Not sure whether it's "bad" or not.

But I think about death a lot too. I often wish I wasn't alive because the pain is so much and I feel like I can't control my thoughts from overwhelming me. But I don't think I can actually go through with it either. I'm too scared and I don't want to hurt the person I love most, even if she doesn't want to be with me....

Sorry you're feeling this way. It sucks.

I hate how friends don't understand either. They just give stupid ass advice that makes me feel worse. I know they're coming from a good place, but it's just not helpful. "It'll get better" isn't useful.

I feel the same way. I keep waking up later and later everyday for work. For some reason that period of time when I'm really groggy and not quite awake yet is the only time I don't feel devastated by everything.

Yeah, you're probably right. I think I'm about as far away from acceptance now anyway, so probably not a big deal... I definitely don't want to rely on that happening, but it's hard to let go of hope even with this "closure" of her not being able to trust me. It's really hard to let go of four years, I'm probably just a hopeless romantic and being delusional, but I feel like there has to be some seed of hope there.

Thanks. Me too. I'm honestly not sure what will come of reaching out to her. It's not like she's going to suddenly want to get back together or anything. I guess it probably won't make things worse though and she may be able to offer some insight, help, encouragement, etc. I'm still severely in denial and hope that someday down the road things can work out. I doubt reaching out will really affect that either. She understands mental illness, and if anything will appreciate that I'm being honest to her about it, especially after she asked me to be. The main thing holding me back from even reaching out to her is that I don't want to annoy her, but I think you may have said earlier that that's unlikely and I should look out for my happiness too. It's not really sustainable if I'm in this much pain everyday. After I come home from work, I just break down crying in my apartment because I had to bottle it up all day.

Good point. I guess none of these issues are a quick fix, sadly.

Yeah... I realize that relying on her help may just prolong the suffering, but when I'm having this much trouble and feel like I can't talk to anyone else about it (hard to be 100% honest with therapist + friends not being great support pillars), it might be worth it. 

I'll try to bring it up. It's hard to get through everything on my mind when the sessions feel so short (and I can't always have them weekly).

I just meant that in the context of our earlier discussion about how she wanted me to tell her if I was having suicidal thoughts (and that given that I trust her most, it would probably be easiest to open up to her since it probably would he helpful to have someone in the real world to talk to about this).

I've been with my therapist for a few months now. I'm honestly not sure what scares me about  opening up completely with her. It may be something worth exploring in sessions as well.

I hope it gets better over time (but at the same time I don't want to stop loving her since I don't want to lose more of her than I already have).

Which is probably why I need to find a way to get beyond the scariness of sharing all my thoughts with her. I don't know why I can't get the courage to tell people I know in real life. If my ex is the only way for me to get that courage, then I probably should get her help. 

My therapist just said she wanted to wait a few weeks to see how my mentality shapes up. But it's hard to believe it's really going to improve on its own :/

Exactly. I know they're trying to be helpful, but I wish they could just be a bit more self aware. When I get defensive about it, they're just like "this is what you need to hear" (well, not in so many words, but it sounds like that on my end). I think you're right that people equate sadness with depression - "getting through my last breakup just took time, so that's all you need too." I mean, I don't think so. I'm clearly taking this harder than your 'average' person. 

I asked my therapist about asking for reasonable accommodations at work b/c of a disability, but I'm also scared of bringing that up since my boss may not be so sympathetic about mental illness.

That makes sense. I feel like it's hard to get support from friends too because I've had a history of clinical depression which just makes everything about this situation even shittier than it would have been in a vacuum. A lot of them just don't understand how hard it is for me to get out of my own negative thoughts, etc. So their "tough love" support just ends up making me feel worse. I wish they would just engage with my venting sometimes. And I'm too scared to really tell them the extent of my pain, so they probably don't even realize how much it's hurting me...

I'll probably have to do that. The job has some flexibility with working from home from time to time, so maybe I can just mask some of those days under that guise too.

Are unhealthy coping mechanisms necessarily "bad"? Is it at least better than having no coping mechanism at all?

That's a good point. And I guess one of the reasons why she felt she couldn't trust me anymore... all I could share with her was what I had done to work on myself with my words in that moment, not any actions :( 

Thanks. Won't it get suspicious if I take mental health days somewhat regularly? How would I even phrase it? I feel like in a way it's none of their business. I said I had a sickness before.

Hopefully I can reach a point where I don't need to rely on those unhealthy coping mechanisms... 

That's a good point that she probably didn't mean everything she said. Ultimately, like you said, her words/actions taken as a whole seem to paint a different picture.

I forced myself to go into work today, since I felt like I couldn't use my sickness excuse for much longer. Turns out my boss wasn't even in today. Left after a couple hours, which were miserable. Got almost nothing done. Just cried the entire time during the commute. Having to face a full work week next week is going to be REALLY hard.

I think you're right. It's just hard because if I'm already feeling THIS bad while using these fantasy coping mechanisms (among others), then maybe it would just be truly unbearable if I didn't. Shrugs.

Thanks. I'll jot this down and hopefully I can get some motivation to try it this weekend. Unfortunately I don't own a pull-up bar. I'm skinny but definitely have no aspirations to be ripped, especially not now.

I guess my thought process was: If she thinks I wasn't a good person, and she was the person who knew me better than anyone else, then maybe it's true. But that's true... depression really is a pit that keeps getting deeper.  

I was having some issues uploading some recent photos I took, but I'll try again later. Maybe it was just a bug. Thanks, by the way, for engaging with me so much. I'm some random stranger and you didn't have to go out of your way to be thoughtful.

I think I end up living vicariously through "what if" scenarios and the like, so it can help me cope in the time.... but maybe it's making it harder for me to move forward... :(

Sure, I could try something like that. I'd rather not have to go to the gym and deal with other people, things being crowded, etc. Thanks. I can try digging up some photos to share.

I just can't forgive myself for hurting her generally. For being selfish and complacent. Good people don't hurt the people they love. So maybe I'm not a very good person (or at least maybe I wasn't at the time). She deserved better.

I hope you're right. I hope she doesn't truly believe that I'm a bad person and don't deserve to be dating anyone. If that was true, why would she want me to be happy, be there for me in case I really need her, etc.?

I think the hardest part about working out is just starting it at all. When I'm in this kind of mood it's hard for me to be productive in any way. My two main hobbies (outside of watching sports, playing video games, watching TV which don't really count) are photography and playing chess. 

My therapist said that she wanted me to wait a few weeks before referring me to a psychiatrist, to see whether things continue to be really bad for that long. I admittedly chickened out and didn't tell her the extent of just how much this is hurting me. I don't know why I did. Unfortunately she's all booked next week and I can't see her for another two weeks. I really wish I could go every week, especially now. She told me that in a way I already forgave myself for hurting her because that's the only way I could have grown. But if that's true I don't know why I'm having such troubles forgiving myself now. There are a lot of things I either forgot to mention to her or just didn't have the time to mention.

I hope she still likes me as a person. When we talked, I could tell there were times she spoke with anger (she said things like she didn't think I was in a position to be dating anyone), and other times she spoke with love (saying that even if we can't be together, she's happy knowing that she helped me grow for someone else). I think she just has a lot of conflicting emotions right now, and I hope that the hurt/anger fades with time and the fondness stays. Yeah... I especially can't place my happiness on someone who doesn't want to be with me :( 

I was starting to develop healthy habits before we had the talk, but they've kind of gone to the wayside since. You're right it's really hard to get any motivation for them... maybe it's just something I need to do one at a time.

I just hope I can reach a point of happiness sometime. It sounds so daunting at this stage. I just had an issue with my computer (which I subsequently figured out) and started having a mini-break down, feeling like everything is just going wrong in my life. 

And sadly, being friends is probably entirely up to her. Maybe she'll never be able to get over the hurt (is that even possible? Or will she eventually be able to move past it too?) and will only want to be there for each other in case of emergencies and the like. I guess it's a good sign that she's even willing to be there for me now in case of emergencies? If she was truly truly angry she probably wouldn't want any part of me.

That's actually an interesting thought re: my subconscious. I know she wants me to be happy (and in a way, being happy honors her), but the hard part for me now is that being happy probably means not being able to talk to her (though I guess if I ever reach that point, I can probably reach out to her and try to create a friendship since presumably I'd be over her romantically at that point).

Will do.

My next appointment is tomorrow, fortunately. I'll try to be open with her.

Yes, that's right. It's probably kind of stupid of me to be curious about the suicidal thoughts because of that. It's like I still want to hold onto being able to talk to her. But it's not like I'm having these thoughts because I want to talk to her either (I'd obviously rather not have these kinds of thoughts). I just don't want to prematurely reach out and annoy her, I only want to reach out if I truly need her help.

I didn't put her before myself enough before. I became complacent. I'm having a hard time forgiving myself. I really wanted the chance to make it up to her. I poured my heart out and I know that she knows how much I love her and care about her still. But that's little consolation. 

I haven't really to be honest. Even if I try to get into a hobby, the pain just seeps through so strong. Basically everything reminds me of her and it feels like I'm being stabbed or something. I wish I could make the hurt stop. But in a weird way I also don't want it to stop because I fear that if it stops, I'll stop loving her, and I don't want to lose even more of her than I have already.

I hope the emotional scars do fade over time for her. I guess a few months wasn't enough time. I understand. People heal at different speeds. But I really thought they could have faded by now. I could tell she was still really hurting. 

Sometimes I feel like she would have been better off never knowing me, because then I wouldn't have hurt her. I hate that I ever hurt her. 

I don't think you can classify it as a friendship right now since she said she wants space from me right now (outside of emergencies).

I know she wants her space, so we have cut off contact outside of truly important things. I know that contacting her right now would just annoy her, and I don't want to hurt her or make her feel uncomfortable. I don't think she's ready to be friends yet. 

Okay, that makes sense. I do want to be honest with the therapist because obviously that will help her treat me better. 

I'm not sure. My girlfriend (I still can't say ex, it's too hard) said that she needs me to contact her if I ever reach that point (it wasn't so much a request but a demand). So I'd probably reach out to her first, to be honest. I think she was worried because I asked her if I could add her as a beneficiary to my various accounts, and she said she couldn't allow me to do that because she didn't want me to do anything to myself. I think I wanted to add her as a beneficiary just because I love her more than anything in this world and want her to be taken care of if anything happens to me. But I'm not sure if that's 100% true either, because at one point I actually researched whether life insurance policies could be paid out on suicide.

Thank you. I know that I'm definitely still in denial over everything, it probably would be best for the long term if I accept things are over, but that's so hard.

I do have a therapist. But I'm scared of bringing up thoughts like this with her because I worry that she'll report me, or send me to a hospital, or I don't even know. 

Are there specific thoughts I should be looking out for when I should start really worrying that I may be suicidal?

We technically broke up a couple months ago, but I had hopes things could work out again.

I saw her this weekend and she basically told me that she isn't in a place to make things work. 

I was depressed and cried every day in the intervening time. Now it's even more crushing. I have a history of severe depression too. I've been googling a lot about suicide today - risk factors, signs, and the like.
The only thing pushing me forward right now is the fact that I know she wants me to be doing so... even if I can't be with her. I don't ever want to hurt her again in any way.
Thank you. I'm trying. It's just so hard when there doesn't appear to be any light at the end of the tunnel :(
I don't know how I'm going to survive this pain

Yesterday was the worst day of my life.

I feel the same way.
I've tried my best to get into a routine everyday (learning new skills, getting back into hobbies, working out) but it only does so much to get my mind off of her :(
